case.question: I fish from the pier for salmon. For this week, how good do you expect pier fishing for salmon to be at each of St. Joseph, South Haven, Grand Haven and Muskegon? Rate each port 0-4 (0 slow, 1 below average, 2 average, 3 good, 4 excellent) and say which you'd go to.

events.text:
## Recommendation

- **Grand Haven pier: 0-1 (slow).** This is the one to try if you go from the pier. Use glow spoons, the only pier lure that caught anything.
- **Muskegon pier: 0 (slow).** Spoons produced no salmon there.
- **South Haven and St. Joseph piers: no pier data.** The reports are boat-only, so I'd expect slow pier fishing there too, roughly 0-1.
- If you can get a boat out, the reports point to 100-200 ft of water with lines at 85-140 ft down, using flies and spoons. Check the wind before you go.

## Why

- The Sept 21 Grand Haven report called pier salmon action slow, with only a few caught on glow spoons.
- The Sept 21 Muskegon report had no salmon from pier anglers casting spoons.
- South Haven and St. Joseph had no pier reports in the last four weeks, so their ratings rest on nearby ports and my own expectation.
- I'd expect the warm nearshore water (about 68 F at Grand Haven and Muskegon, satellite) to keep salmon deeper and offshore, which fits the slow pier reports.

## Evidence

**Recent reports** (newest is Sept 21, six days old)
- Grand Haven, 2026-09-21 (dated 2022-09-21 in the database): pier "slow," quality 0, "a few were caught on glow spoons." Boats did better: quality 3, fish 85-140 ft down in 100-200 ft of water, on white-paddle flies and green spoons.
- Muskegon, 2022-09-21: pier quality 0, "No salmon were reported from pier anglers casting spoons." Boats were quality 3, fish 85-130 ft down in 130-210 ft.
- South Haven, 2022-09-21: no pier entry. Boats were quality 2, best water beyond 120 ft, most fish on spoons.
- St. Joseph, 2022-09-21: no pier entry. Boats were quality 2, best water around 120 ft.
- Earlier pier reports in September (Grand Haven 2022-09-14 and 09-07, Muskegon 09-07) were also all quality 0.

**Past seasons** (history, not current)
- Similar-water weeks at St. Joseph and South Haven (about 67 F surface) returned only the Sept 21, 2022 St. Joseph boat report (quality 2). Nothing about piers.
- No past weeks matched Grand Haven or Muskegon's buoy temperature (62 F) within 6 F, so I have no history for those ports at this temperature.

**Conditions now**
- The conditions check returned a backtest summary for the week before Sept 27, not live data.
- Grand Haven and Muskegon pier-area satellite water: about 68 F, down 4-5 F in the last three days. Wind was upwelling-favoring for 33-37 hours in those three days.
- The Grand Haven and Muskegon buoy (45029) read 62 F, down 21 F over the week. That drop is unusually large and may be a sensor problem.
- South Haven and St. Joseph satellite water was about 68 F, down 3-4 F in the last three days.

## Caveats

- The newest report is from Sept 21, six days before today. Treat these ratings as a guide, since fall conditions change fast.
- The conditions data is a backtest summary, not live. The satellite and buoy temperatures are measured, but the upwelling read is an inference from wind and temperature change.
- South Haven and St. Joseph have no pier reports in four weeks, so their ratings are my expectation.
- Pier catches are sparse in every recent report, so even Grand Haven at 0-1 is a weak forecast.

- Sept 14 DNR report: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/32cff90 (context only)
- Sept 7 DNR report: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/32bbcf0 (context only)
